chunks: He sends [a messenger] to her, and the messenger says: 'Begin your waiting period ('iddah), for so-and-so has separated from you.'

key_terms.اعتدّي: 'Iddah — the obligatory waiting period a divorced woman must observe before remarrying, typically three menstrual cycles
key_terms.الرسول: Al-Rasul — the messenger/envoy; here referring to the person delegated to deliver the divorce
key_terms.فارقكِ: Farāqa — 'separated/parted from you'; one of the valid formulas for pronouncing divorce in Shia fiqh

ai.seo_question: Is divorce by proxy valid in Shia Islam, and what words constitute a valid divorce formula?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that divorce by proxy is valid: a husband may send a messenger to his wife to deliver the divorce formula and instruct her to begin her obligatory waiting period ('iddah). The formula 'so-and-so has separated from you' (fāraqa-ki) constitutes a valid expression of divorce according to Shia jurisprudence, even without the husband being physically present. This ruling addresses a practical scenario of divorce that was common in classical Islamic society where communication was conducted through intermediaries.
